correctness.rationale: Definition and quantifiers are explicit. Every nonresolving set lies in a pair bisector. The exact one-cycle distance-difference histograms cover all nonzero shifts for both parities. Majorization, rearrangement and alignment of shift-one supports prove the global sharp bound for pairs moving in both coordinates. Zero-coordinate cases are solved separately. Elementary comparisons cover all orders and identify the 4-cycle exception, and the stated pairs attain every maximum. Checker independently tested all offsets on 1444 graphs and shortest paths/vertex pairs on 64, with VERIFY_OK; finite tests are supplementary, not an infinite proof.

value.rationale: The least number of arbitrarily placed landmarks guaranteeing unique localization is a natural robustness invariant. The result completely determines it on all rectangular cycle-product tori, sharply distinguishes parity regimes and exposes a genuinely exceptional length-four factor. This is more informative than the minimum metric dimension, and the histogram-majorization proof supplies a reusable method for distance-product bisector maximization.
